seoTitle: Add a Payment Method in Hostinger Store Manager
metaDescription: Connect PayPal, Stripe, or a local payment processor to your Hostinger eCommerce store so you can accept payments.
intro: Linking a payment method is the step that turns a Hostinger website from a page people can browse into a store that can actually take money. The setting lives inside Store Manager's Payments section, and connecting a provider like Stripe involves a real verification step, not just typing in a few settings. This guide walks through logging in, finding the payment settings inside Store Manager, and completing the Stripe verification screen you'll actually see during setup.

steps.heading: Log in to your Hostinger account
steps.body: Open hostinger.com in your browser and click Log in at the top right. Sign in with your Hostinger credentials to reach hPanel, the control panel where hosting, domains, and store settings all live. If you're new, you'll see promotional offers for hosting and AI website tools on the homepage first — none of that is required to set up payments, so head straight for the login button rather than getting pulled into a plan upgrade.

image.caption: The Hostinger homepage with the Log in button in the top-right corner, where the payment setup process starts.

steps.heading: Open Store Manager for your site
steps.body: From hPanel, find the website running your store and open its Store Manager. You'll land on an overview page with a "Set up your store" checklist tracking your progress — items like adding your first product, setting up a payment method, and updating your company information, each with a checkmark once done. This checklist is a useful sanity check: if "Set up a payment method" already shows a green checkmark, a gateway is already connected, and you're here to change or add one rather than set up from scratch.

image.caption: The Store Manager overview with its setup checklist, showing "Set up a payment method" already marked complete.

steps.heading: Navigate to Settings, then Payments
steps.body: In the left-hand sidebar, click Settings to expand it, which reveals Store details, Company information, Payments, Shipping, Checkout, Emails, Taxes, and Invoices. Click Payments — this is the section where you add, edit, or remove the gateways your store accepts. It's easy to go looking for this under a top-level "Payments" menu item instead, but in Store Manager it sits nested under Settings alongside the store's other configuration pages.

image.caption: The expanded Settings menu in Store Manager, with Payments listed alongside Shipping, Checkout, and Taxes.

steps.heading: Connect a provider and complete verification
steps.body: Choose a supported gateway — Stripe is built directly into Hostinger's Website Builder for secure payments, and PayPal or a local processor may also be available depending on your region. When you connect Stripe specifically, expect a real identity verification step: a "Verify your login" screen asking for a 6-digit code from your authenticator app before the connection completes. This isn't optional friction to skip past — it's Stripe confirming you're the account holder before it starts routing customer payments through your store, so have your authenticator app ready before you start this step.

image.caption: The Stripe verification screen shown when connecting payments through Hostinger Website Builder, asking for a 6-digit authenticator code.

steps.heading: Pick the gateway that fits your customers
steps.body: If more than one option is available, choose based on where your customers actually are rather than which provider you've heard of most. Stripe and PayPal both cover a wide range of countries and cards, but local processors sometimes offer lower fees or faster payouts in specific regions, and some customers trust a familiar local brand at checkout more than an international one. You can typically enable more than one gateway at once, letting customers pick their preferred option at checkout instead of forcing everyone through a single processor.

steps.heading: Confirm it's live before you announce the store
steps.body: Once the connection is saved, go back to the Store Manager overview and confirm the payment method checklist item now shows complete. Before sending real traffic to the store, place a small test order if your provider supports test mode, or check the provider's own dashboard to confirm the store is correctly linked to your account. Catching a misconfigured gateway before launch is far less painful than finding out from a customer whose checkout failed.

faq.question: Which payment methods does Hostinger's Store Manager support?
faq.answer: Stripe is built directly into Hostinger Website Builder for secure payments, and PayPal or other local or custom gateways may also be available depending on your location.

faq.question: Where is the Store Manager located?
faq.answer: Open hPanel after logging in, find the website running your store, and open its Store Manager. Payment settings live under Settings → Payments inside that view.

faq.question: Do I need to verify my identity to connect Stripe?
faq.answer: Yes. When connecting Stripe through Hostinger Website Builder, you'll be asked to enter a 6-digit verification code from your authenticator app before the connection is completed.

faq.question: Why is adding a payment method important for a Hostinger store?
faq.answer: It's the core requirement for turning website traffic into actual revenue by letting customers pay for what they order — without it, products can be browsed but not purchased.

faq.question: Can I use more than one payment gateway at once?
faq.answer: Typically yes — many stores enable both an international option like Stripe or PayPal and a local processor, letting customers choose their preferred method at checkout.
